v1.feedback: The Mohr→hypercube conceptual link is genuinely strong — Mohr literally pioneered 4D cube art, so 'bloom-burst' as organic flowering of his geometry is a smart swerve. The quantized positions (PS=0.35 grid snap) honor the pixel/computational lineage well. Two things to refine: the fill-dust particles (random scatter in the 28×28×24 box) dilute the tesseract's clean silhouette — cut them to ≤15% of budget or confine them to a tight halo around the edges so the hypercube reads instantly. Second, the bloom petals (fibonacci-sphere burst at each vertex) risk reading as uniform fuzzballs at 180 petals per vertex; elongate them along the adjacent edge directions so each bloom has directional 'sepals' that echo the cube geometry rather than generic spheres.

v2.feedback: Strong concept — Mohr hypercube flowering into organic sepals is a genuine surprise swerve that honors the parent lineage. Palette (ash/amber-rust on near-black) is well-restrained. Two refinements: the 0.35 quantization grid makes bloom petals read as chunky voxel stubs rather than organic forms — consider halving the grid step for ptype===2 particles so the flowering reads as a finer, more delicate eruption from the rigid lattice. The dust halo (15% budget, 1.8-unit spread) softens the silhouette more than it helps — tighten spread to ≤0.8 or reallocate those particles to denser petal geometry so the bloom moment carries more visual weight.
